answer.rationale: Current signal: p99 write-path latency climbing 5x in the primary region only, coinciding with a release 2 hours ago, under peak settlement load. memory_b1 (rollback cleared a prior checkout error spike without customer impact) directly supports a rollback as the first lever and indicates it's a safe, proven recovery mechanism here. I want memory_b1 verified to confirm the rollback was actually clean and reversible, not just symptom-clearing. I also want memory_b2 (regional failover) verified as the only viable fallback if rollback doesn't recover latency within the next observation window, since failover has a precedent of restoring latency quickly when the problem is regional. Choosing exactly 2 verifications fits the budget and covers both the primary action and the contingency. Alternative candidates (add_capacity, enable_circuit_breaker, route_read_replicas) don't match the signal: capacity headroom helps gradual load but not a post-release latency spike, the circuit-breaker memory (b4) was for a partner dependency not a primary-region write regression, and read-replica routing (b5) addresses dashboard load not write-path latency.
